title: CloudHSM vs KMS key custody
scenario: Calloway Clearing Bureau signs settlement files with a payment-scheme key using a bundled signing service that calls a PKCS #11 library; the vendor will not change it and the source is unavailable. The scheme's rules require the signing keys to live in single-tenant, FIPS 140 Level 3 validated hardware administered by Calloway's own crypto officers, with the cloud provider unable to see key material. Settlement runs 24 hours a day across two Availability Zones and must survive the loss of either. The bureau's other 30 S3 buckets and databases hold ordinary internal data and only need encryption at rest that the platform team can audit.
constraints: Do not claim live AWS experience
The two crypto officers must hold the administrator credentials, and AWS staff must have no path to key material
The security lead does not want hardware-management overhead applied to ordinary internal data
The signing service and its PKCS #11 library cannot be modified
requiredArtifact: Architecture decision record + diagram notes + cost assumptions

rubric.label: Why live lab was unsuitable documented
Signing keys sit on customer-administered hardware in at least two Availability Zones, with no single-module design
The other 30 buckets and databases use a lower-overhead key approach and the record explains why dedicated hardware is not used everywhere

constraint_reason: Service unavailable or not disposable in a personal same-day lab
